+title: 'Filter agent: the write, parse and correct loop, with a scripted model'
+---
+## What
+
+Fill the translator seam of `translateFilter` with the loop of the filter agent (divergence.md §17, "The loop" and "No memory").
+
+- Each call makes a new `LanguageModelSession` with the `filterModel`, the system prompt resource and the board vocabulary.
+- The model writes one statement. The engine parses it with `FilterParser` and runs the name check.
+- A parse error or an unknown name goes back to the model as the `INVALID_FILTER` message (the position, the specific message and the corrected example). The model writes again in the same session.
+- At most 3 attempts. The first statement that parses and passes the name check is the result: `{ filter, attempts: n }`.
+- After 3 failed attempts: `filter` is null, `message` gives the last error, `attempts` is 3.
+- An error of the model itself (for example, the model is not available) gives a clear error. It does not count as an attempt.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] A correct statement at once gives `attempts: 1`.
+- [ ] A parse error and then a correction gives `attempts: 2`, and the second prompt holds the `INVALID_FILTER` message.
+- [ ] An unknown name and then a correction gives `attempts: 2`.
+- [ ] 3 failed attempts give `filter: null`, the last error in `message`, and `attempts: 3`. There is no 4th call.
+- [ ] Two calls do not share a session.
+
+## Tests
+
+- Unit tests in `T/` with a scripted `LanguageModel` that gives a fixed list of answers and records each prompt.
+- `swift test` passes with no new warnings. #kanbanviewkit #filter-agent
\ No newline at end of file

+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Filter/FilterAgentLoop.swift:85` `completeness/public-output-contract` — stoppingTheAgent converts every error from the model into KanbanError.filterAgentFailed, including CancellationError. When the caller cancels the call, the error that reaches the caller is a user-facing FILTER_AGENT_FAILED message that tells the caller to send the call again, not a cancellation. The cancelled call is then reported as a model failure, which hides the cancellation from the caller. Rethrow CancellationError unchanged, or check Task.isCancelled in the catch block, so that only real model and prompt-resource failures become FILTER_AGENT_FAILED. Add a test that cancels the call and checks that the error is not FILTER_AGENT_FAILED.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Filter/FilterAgentLoop.swift:144` `completeness/invariant-propagation` — withoutCodeSpan removes the first and last backtick of any text that starts and ends with a backtick. It does not check that the text is a code span. A text that is a code fence with no line break, or a span that wraps a label, loses one mark at each end and still fails the parse. The docstring says the forgiving read handles a code span, but a span that wraps a label ('`Filter: #bug`') is not handled, because the label step runs before the span step. Strip the span before the label, or repeat all the steps until nothing changes. Add one test case for a span that wraps a label, and one for a single-line fenced statement.

-- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Filter/FilterAgentLoop.swift:85` `completeness/public-output-contract` — stoppingTheAgent converts every error from the model into KanbanError.filterAgentFailed, including CancellationError. When the caller cancels the call, the error that reaches the caller is a user-facing FILTER_AGENT_FAILED message that tells the caller to send the call again, not a cancellation. The cancelled call is then reported as a model failure, which hides the cancellation from the caller. Rethrow CancellationError unchanged, or check Task.isCancelled in the catch block, so that only real model and prompt-resource failures become FILTER_AGENT_FAILED. Add a test that cancels the call and checks that the error is not FILTER_AGENT_FAILED.
-- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsKanban/Filter/FilterAgentLoop.swift:144` `completeness/invariant-propagation` — withoutCodeSpan removes the first and last backtick of any text that starts and ends with a backtick. It does not check that the text is a code span. A text that is a code fence with no line break, or a span that wraps a label, loses one mark at each end and still fails the parse. The docstring says the forgiving read handles a code span, but a span that wraps a label ('`Filter: #bug`') is not handled, because the label step runs before the span step. Strip the span before the label, or repeat all the steps until nothing changes. Add one test case for a span that wraps a label, and one for a single-line fenced statement.
